decisions_for_user.question: Does an-archived-agent-holds-nothing-and-is-offered-nowhere accept a hub/ui/src bundle refresh, or ship API-only?
decisions_for_user.context: WIDENED BY R2 into one decision with two halves, both the same wall (a hub/ui/src change -> make ui -> reaches the operator's live :8000 app). Half (a), found by R1: the change makes PATCH /agents/{name} refuse binding a charter to an archived agent, but the archived agent's Charter section keeps rendering CharterPicker (AgentSettingsPage.tsx:124-135) and on failure shows only its own generic 'Could not update charter binding.' -- the server's sentence is dropped, the F187 shape. Half (b), found by R2: nothing renders the archive or unarchive response AT ALL -- useArchiveAgent (hub/ui/src/api/agents.ts:214-241) is the only client of both routes and its onSuccess takes no argument, so the body is discarded. So every sentence group 2 adds (released_charter_id, the archive sentence, the unarchive standing sentence) is an API fact no operator can read, and the operator's own rider ('unarchive must then say the bindings are gone') is only half discharged. The change is complete and shippable without either half. R3 (iteration 5) did not change either half, but found a THIRD option neither earlier round had: archiving persists no event at all (F391, design.md D10), so a persist_event(..., 'agent_archived', {released_charter_id: ...}) would make the released binding DURABLE and queryable with NO hub/ui/src change and therefore no bundle refresh -- the only route to the rider's second half that does not reach the live :8000 app. It does not render it (useSSE.ts allow-lists event kinds at :31 and switches at :460), so it closes the recording gap, not the display gap.
options: accept the bundle refresh and do both halves (disable the picker + surface the server detail; render what archive/unarchive say)
accept the bundle refresh for half (a) only
ship API-only and file both halves as their own findings
ship API-only now, and take F391's server-side event separately -- makes the released charter durable without a bundle refresh, but still renders nothing
